findings.checklist_item: Name the concrete Gerrit-posting mechanism that carries the summarize() TEXT to the patchset (gerrit-review-action provably cannot per the plan's own evidence) — e.g. a trusted SSH `gerrit review --message "<summary>"` step — and reconcile AC4's `comment-only: true` assertion with it.
evidence: Plan quote: 'It exposes no input for custom text.'
Plan quote: 'the detail must be posted as an ADDITIONAL comment-only review on the same patchset.'
AC4: 'a step using comment-only: true guarded on the vote-type' — comment-only is a gerrit-review-action input, and that action self-builds `MESSAGE="${STATUS}: .../runs/${RUN_ID}"`
search_files for 'gerrit review --message' and 'ssh' in gerrit-verify.yaml returned no matches: no alternative text-capable poster exists in the repo today
findings.finding: The chosen mechanism cannot carry the summary text to Gerrit: the plan's own evidence shows gerrit-review-action builds its message as `STATUS: url` and 'exposes no input for custom text', but Approach step 2 and AC4 post the summary via a `comment-only: true` step of that same action — which would post `STATUS: url` again, not the triage summary. No text-capable Gerrit poster (e.g. a direct SSH `gerrit review --message`) is named.
findings.location: Approach step 2; AC4; 'Why the message is empty today'
scenarios: A cancelled/timed-out run: the vote job runs the comment-only gerrit-review-action step, which posts a second `CANCELLED: <url>` message and never the per-job summary — the observability goal is not met.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the comment-only gerrit-review-action step with a dedicated SSH step (the same `ssh ... gerrit review --message` the action uses internally, using the existing GERRIT_* vars/secret) that posts summarize()'s output with no label, guarded on `steps.normalize.outputs.vote-type != 'success'`; update AC4 to assert that step.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete mechanism that delivers summarize()'s text to Gerrit (e.g. a raw `ssh -p 29418 <user>@<host> gerrit review --message <file> <change>,<patchset>` step, or an action input that actually accepts a message body), since gerrit-review-action's comment-only:true carries no custom text; if none is confirmed available with the SSH-key-only CI account, route this to a spike before committing.
evidence: Plan: 'It exposes no input for custom text.' and 'Its inputs are host, port, username, key, key_name, known_hosts, gerrit-change-number, gerrit-patchset-number, vote-type, comment-only.'
AC4: 'Asserted by a test parsing gerrit-verify.yaml for a step using comment-only: true guarded on the vote-type.' — ties delivery to the same action that has no message input.
gerrit-review-action's cast is `review --message "<STATUS>: <server>/<repo>/actions/runs/<run_id>"` (gerrit-verify.yaml lines 374-380) — the message is action-generated, not caller-supplied.
ADR-0023: the CI account is SSH-key-only with 'no HTTP password', so a REST comment path is unavailable without new credential provisioning.
findings.finding: The plan's only named mechanism for posting the triage summary to Gerrit — a gerrit-review-action step with comment-only:true — cannot carry the arbitrary text summarize() produces, because (by the plan's own analysis) that action 'exposes no input for custom text' and always builds its own '<STATUS>: <url>' message. The delivery mechanism for the enriched comment is therefore unspecified/infeasible as written.
findings.location: Approach step 2; AC4; "Why the message is empty today"
scenarios: A cancelled/timed-out run: the vote job runs the comment-only step, which posts the action's own 'CANCELLED: <url>' text again instead of the summarize() triage lines — no observability gain shipped.
Implementer discovers at build time that comment-only:true only suppresses the label but still emits the built-in message, with no `comment`/`message` input to override it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the summary+comment step is best-effort (e.g. `continue-on-error: true` or an internal try/guard) so a failure to fetch jobs/annotations or post the Gerrit comment never fails the vote job or alters the +1/-1 cast.
evidence: 'In `vote`, when the normalized vote-type is not `success`, run that script over this run's jobs and post the result to Gerrit as a comment-only review'
'When the gate votes +1 or -1 must not change; only what the -1 message carries.'
ABSENCE: no failure-handling / best-effort disposition stated for the new API reads and Gerrit POST
findings.finding: The plan adds new failure points to the vote job (a GitHub list-jobs API read, a check-run annotations read requiring the new `checks: read` scope, and a Gerrit comment-only review POST) but does not state what happens if the summary or comment step fails. The stated invariant is that '+1 or -1 must not change'; if the added step can fail the job, an API/Gerrit error would change the observable outcome of a run that previously voted cleanly.
findings.location: Approach step 2 / Files (vote job: add summary + comment step)
scenarios: A cancel/timeout run triggers the summary step; the GitHub list-jobs API or the Gerrit comment POST errors, the added step fails, and the vote job that would have cast -1 now errors — changing behavior the plan says must not change
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach step 2: the summary/comment step runs with continue-on-error (or wraps its own failures) so the vote cast is unaffected, and add an AC asserting the step does not gate the vote.

The existing vote job uses im-open/workflow-conclusion for its own list-jobs read, but the plan does not state that step exposes the raw payload, nor how annotations (a separate per-check-run API) are gathered

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin down the timeout-detection capability: state which annotation surface summarize() reads (job vs check-run annotations, and how job↔annotation are correlated) and justify that a case-insensitive substring match on 'exceeded the maximum execution time' covers BOTH observed wordings ('...of 30m0s' and '...running on runner ... of N minutes'), citing the retrieved GitHub annotation forms.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'whether it TIMED OUT (annotation "exceeded the maximum execution time")'
Plan Evidence quotes: 'The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 30m0s'

Retrieved web sources (github.com community discussion 50430, Stack Overflow 68187987) show the alternative wild form: 'The job running on runner GitHub Actions X has exceeded the maximum execution time of N minutes'
GitHub Docs (rest/checks/runs) confirms annotations are read per-check-run via the checks:read permission the plan adds
findings.finding: The timeout-detection capability rests on matching the check-run annotation substring 'exceeded the maximum execution time', but the observed annotation text is not a stable contract: the plan's own Evidence quotes 'The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 30m0s' while GitHub's more commonly documented runner annotation reads 'The job running on runner GitHub Actions X has exceeded the maximum execution time of N minutes'. Both happen to contain the chosen phrase, so the approach works, but the plan asserts the timeout signal without pinning down which annotation surface it reads or acknowledging the wording varies (per-minute vs Nm0s, and 'checks' annotations vs the job's own annotations).
scenarios: A future GitHub Actions annotation-wording change (or a runner that emits the 'running on runner ...' variant) silently reclassifies a real timeout as a plain cancel, defeating the whole triage-signal purpose
The annotation the summarizer reads is attached to a check-run, not the job; if the mapping from job to its annotation is ambiguous the timeout gets attributed to the wrong job or dropped
